figures.finding: Bermuda, a British Overseas Territory with its own tax laws, levies no income tax on individuals; pay is taxed instead by payroll tax, whose employee portion runs from 0.25% on the first BMD 48,000 a year to 12.5% on 500,001 to 1,000,000, nothing above.
figures.applies: Employee portion, 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027, applied to the annual rate of pay; the employer may deduct it from pay but is liable for it.

sources.said: Since income taxes are not imposed on individuals in Bermuda, income tax rates are not relevant in the context of Bermuda taxation.

Payroll Tax, levied under the Payroll Tax Act 1995 and the Payroll Tax Rates Act 1995 , is a tax on all employers, self-employed persons, and deemed employees on the remuneration paid in their business.

Employers have the option to deduct the employee portion of payroll tax from employees however the responsibility to pay the full amount of tax (i.e. employer plus employee portions) rests with the employer.

figures.finding: Payroll tax runs on a year from 1 April to 31 March, paid quarterly on 15 January, 15 April, 15 July and 15 October; individuals file no income tax return.

sources.said: Payroll Tax must be paid in Bermuda on 15 January, 15 April, 15 July, and 15 October every year.
EMPLOYEE PORTION TAX RATES APRIL 1, 2026 - MARCH 31, 2027
Since income taxes are not imposed on individuals in Bermuda, tax returns are not required to be completed for individual income tax compliance purposes .

figures.finding: The employer pays a payroll tax employer portion by size and class (0.5% under BMD 200,000 of payroll up to 9.5% above 1,000,000; 9.75% for exempted undertakings); social insurance is a flat weekly contribution, from 1 August 2026 BMD 39.25 from the employee and 39.25 from the employer (only the employer's 39.25 past 65), and a self-employed person pays 78.50 (39.25 past 65).
figures.applies: Payroll tax from 1 April 2026; social insurance as reported by PwC in October 2026 (the latest primary notice found is the 2018 increase to 71.84).

sources.said: Taxpayers with an annual payroll less than $200,000 (or less than $50,000 p/qtr.) 0.5%
Taxpayers with an annual payroll greater than $1,000,000 p/a (>$250,000 p/qtr.) 9.50% All Exempt Undertakings 9.75%

figures.finding: Nothing is withheld for income tax; the employer may deduct the employee portion of payroll tax and the employee's social insurance from pay.

sources.said: Employers have the option to deduct the employee portion of payroll tax from employees

figures.finding: A foreign performer or contractor working in Bermuda pays no income tax; foreign contractors and subcontractors must pay payroll tax on remuneration for services provided in Bermuda.

value.payrollTax: applies to foreign contractors and subcontractors

sources.said: Foreign contractors and subcontractors in Bermuda must also pay Payroll Tax.
Taxable remuneration includes the sum of wages/salaries and benefits paid in cash or in kind to employees, self-employed persons, and deemed employees as a result of services provided in Bermuda.

figures.finding: Bermuda has no VAT or sales tax.

sources.said: There is no VAT or sales tax in Bermuda.

figures.finding: A musician or other entertainer is, for each performance, the employee of whoever engages him, whatever the contract says, so the engager accounts for payroll tax on his pay; a Bermudian musician or entertainer pays 0% employee payroll tax on that pay.

value.deemedEmployee: musician or other entertainer, of the person engaging him, per performance

figures.applies: Musicians and other entertainers engaged in Bermuda; the 0% rate for those with Bermudian status, from 1 April 2019

sources.said: A musician or other entertainer (whether or not, apart from this subsection, he is the employee of any other person) is for the purposes of this Act, as respects any performance for which he is engaged by any person (regardless of the terms of the engagement), the employee of the latter person and not of any other person. … a Bermudian musician or other entertainer shall not be liable to payroll tax at the employee's standard rate in relation to his remuneration as a musician or entertainer, but shall instead be charged at the rate prescribed in the Rates Act for the purposes of this section.
Bermudian musicians and other entertainers … 0% is prescribed as the rate for the purposes of section 9D.
